meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so you have twenty minutes. My son found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, and when?
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Was my son given a chance to speak before you entered it? And on what basis did you enter it at all?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.

Turn the screen, Hale; I'll read those times myself, and I'm writing down 11:31, 11:52 and 11:58. People paste from their own notes every day, so a big edit tells you when the words arrived, not who wrote them. And you still haven't told me whether my son was heard before that zero went in.
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
Show me the scene. A misquoted line costs marks, Hale; it doesn't make a zero. Before you say another word, whatever happens next, nothing goes on his record and nobody in that class hears about it.

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

Who decides whether it "holds up," Hale, and on what standard? I'll want all of that in an email tonight, including a sentence that nothing is on his file right now and nothing goes on it. And who else in this building knows about this besides you and the vice-principal?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you acknowledged that the zero was entered before I was contacted, and you offered Owen a supervised rewrite in your room on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal supervising, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require written confirmation that nothing is on Owen's file now or will be, the standard by which the rewrite will be judged, the names of everyone who knows about this, and an assurance that none of it reaches his class. I expect that email from you tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: fallback position, weighing the supervised rewrite but agreeing to nothing until she had its terms in writing.
What moved her: the quotation that isn't in Hamlet, backed by the version-history timestamps.
